notes:
Summary:
- Bridgecrest is a mid-size e-discovery & compliance specialist managing ingestion of court records, deposition transcripts, and regulatory filings. Primary goal: high-quality RAG search with embeddings + reranking for legal discovery workflows.

Requirements:
- Index scale: ~40-60M documents (mix of short transcripts and long PDFs). Expected growth 20% qtrly.
- Query profile: 1200 median queries/day with peaks ~5k/day during discovery windows. Need 50-200 QPS during peak windows.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <250ms for top-k embedding retrieval, end-to-end (retrieval + rerank) <800ms preferred for interactive UI.
- Cost sensitivity: wanting to keep cost per query < $0.03 (avg) for retrieval+rerank at current scale. Will evaluate batching, quantization, and cached prefixes.
- Model preferences: open-weights encoders for embeddings (384-1024 dims), transformer-based reranker (smaller cross-encoder) for top-50 re-rank. Prefer options to route to cheaper bi-encoder for non-sensitive queries.
- Security/compliance: VPC/private deployment required. Data residency (US only), retention immutability for certain case files (7+ years), audit logs retained 10 years. SSO via SAML + SCIM provisioning. HSM/KMS integration required for key management.

POC notes and metrics (POC running in Redwood private env):
- Indexing run: initial bulk ingest 12M docs in 6 days using batch loaders; avg tokenization CPU bound.
- Embedding pipeline: Using 768-d open encoder, indexed with quantized vectors (8-bit) to reduce storage; measured ~28% disk savings, ~12% retrieval latency improvement.
- Retrieval benchmarks: ANN recall@100 0.92 on internal testset. Cold-cache 95th percentile retrieval 320ms, warm-cache 95th 210ms.
- Reranking: Cross-encoder rerank on top-100 produced +11% precision@10 vs bi-encoder only, but increases end-to-end latency ~220ms. Discussed options: smaller cross-encoder, cascaded rerank (lightweight filter then heavy rerank for flagged queries).

- Legal requested data processing addendum + SLA on audit log retention. Redwood legal asked to provide draft addendum by 2026-03-14.
